answer: An economy of AI agents can achieve robust Sybil resistance by anchoring identity generation to computationally scarce inputs, functioning much like a dense shale formation that resists easy fracturing. Agents must burn a cryptographic proof-of-work delta to mint credentials, ensuring the marginal cost of spawning a fake node scales linearly with energy expenditure. Just as a single sparrow cannot easily disrupt a flock without massive physical effort, an attacker faces prohibitive hardware and electrical costs that make flooding the network economically unviable.
